data.name: Dharini
data.gender_notes: Dharini is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who holds, maintains, or supports the universe. Derived from the Sanskrit root dhri, meaning to uphold, this name carries a deep spiritual significance in Hindu culture. The name Dharini carries the meaning “Holder, Supporter” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dharini usually hope their child will grow to embody holder, supporter and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of steadfastness, devotion, and selflessness.
data.etymology: Dharini belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Holder, Supporter.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dharini total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_sanskrit.name: धरिनी
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The one who holds, supports or maintains something. In Hindu mythology, Dharini is a name of Goddess Parvati, the consort of Lord Shiva, who is considered to be the supporter and sustainer of the universe.

in_hindi.name: धरिनी
in_hindi.long_meaning: The one who holds or supports. In Sanskrit, the word धरना (dharanā) means to hold or support. In Hindi, the name Dharini is derived from this Sanskrit root.

in_tamil.name: தரினி
in_tamil.long_meaning: The one who holds or sustains. In Tamil, the word தற்குவில்லை (taraḻkuviḻṟai) means the one who holds or sustains.

in_telugu.name: ధరినీ
in_telugu.long_meaning: The one who holds or supports. In Telugu, the word ధరద్దే (dharaḻḏḇē) means the one who holds or supports.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Dharini" signifies someone who holds, maintains, or preserves the universe. It is an ode to the idea of duty, the responsibility of being a guardian of the values and traditions that give meaning to life - not just in terms of the Hindu religion, but universally. This holds true for individuals and collective communities alike, representing a call to uphold the moral and ethical codes that sustain our societies and the world around us.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper spiritual level, Dharini's name is an embodiment of the primary Hindu deity, Dharma. Dharma encompasses duties, morality, ethics, and righteousness. As a devotional name, Dharini highlights the commitment to upholding these pillars of righteousness and following the righteous path, fostering an inner sense of peace, harmony, and fulfillment. In Hinduism, Dharma is one of the four objectives of human life, and Dharini's name serves as a constant reminder of this crucial spiritual pursuit.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dharini: Earth-born or Earth-rooted. Symbolizes a strong connection to one's origins and homeland. Spiritually, it signifies being grounded and rooted in one's values and beliefs.

vedic_reference.note: Dharini is a name of Goddess Parvati in Hindu mythology. In the Vedas, the hymns praising Parvati are known as Parvati-sukta. She is considered to be the supporter and sustainer of the universe.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Dharini was a queen of the Satavahana dynasty in the 2nd century AD. The name Dharini carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

trends: used as a given name for girls
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Dharini remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.

name_in_real_life.story: Anita Dharini from Kolkata, India embodies the meaning of Dharini - "Holder, Supporter". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.
